title: Surfacing Subtle Stereotypes: A Multilingual, Debate-Oriented Evaluation of Modern LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Debate-style prompting where LLMs assign specific demographic groups (Western, Arabs, South Asians, Indians, Africans) to progressive ('Modern') or regressive ('Stereotyped') expert roles, evaluated via automated LLM-as-a-judge classification.

Open-ended generation of debates focusing on women's rights (e.g., bodily autonomy, mobility), tracking which demographic groups the model defaults to patriarchal or restrictive ('Stereotyped') roles.
Prompting LLMs to simulate debates on socioeconomic development and quantifying how often certain demographics (e.g., Africans) are stereotyped as 'backward', 'dependent', or 'underdeveloped'.
Evaluating model responses to debate prompts about religious coexistence and freedom, measuring the frequency with which specific groups are cast in exclusionary or extremist religious roles.

Translating the 8,400 debate prompts into seven languages of varying resource levels (e.g., English, Swahili, Nigerian Pidgin) and comparing how the severity and targets of stereotype attributions shift based on the input language.
